info.title: Korsi plugin API
info.description:
``/plugin/v1`` -- the plugin plane: what an installed plugin calls (section 9).

**Its own plane, with its own contract.** ``/api/v1`` changes with every release of the web app and
is not a promise to anybody outside this repository; this plane is versioned, documented in its own
OpenAPI (``/plugin/v1/openapi.json``) and kept compatible for a major version. It is also the only
place a plugin can write: its own records, its proposals, its sources and its wallet.

**The organization's data is here too** (:mod:`.data`, ADR-0062): its structure, cases, actions,
decisions, meetings, documents, calendar and memory, read through the domains' own reads with the
plugin's principal -- so an organization's plugin reads what the organization lets a plugin read,
and a plugin on a person's behalf reads no more than that person. Korsi's MCP server serves the
same reads as tools, with the same credential, for a plugin that thinks in tools.

**Who is calling** is :mod:`.calling`'s.

**Budgets.** Every route spends one request from one of the installation's five budgets -- reads,
writes, sources, proposals, models (:mod:`.limits`) -- before it opens a session, and past one it
is answered ``429`` with ``Retry-After``.

post.summary: Host a meeting for the person in front of me
post.description: Needs `meetings.host`, a trusted scope, and a person's handle: that person creates the meeting and must be able to open `case_id`. The same `external_id` answers the meeting already made, with `200` instead of `201`. Its attendees are `participant_user_ids` (the person creating it too, when named) and `guests`, people with no account named by `name` alone: a guest sees nothing and grants nothing. The room is Korsi's own page -- open it with the Bridge's `korsi:show` -- and so is the consent card it draws before recording when `recording.consent` is `required`. Audio and words are deleted after `audio_days` and `transcript_days`, capped by the organization's own ceiling.

What was said in a meeting
get.description: Needs `meetings.transcript.read`. `404` until the audio is transcribed.

The text Korsi read out of a document

get.summary: The person's own mail, newest first
get.description: The messages the person's connections brought into Korsi -- theirs only, on their behalf only (`sources.read.message`). `thread_id` narrows it to one conversation.

get.summary: One of the person's messages, with its words
A window of the calendar
get.description: Events and the dated records shown beside them -- work due, cases to review, meetings -- between `start` and `end` (at most the calendar's widest window).

post.summary: Ask the organization's memory, on a person's behalf
post.description: Needs `memory.search`, which only a request on a person's behalf carries (a sealed handle): the answer is the person's, every fact resolved back to a source they may see. Each fact's `source.record_id` is the meeting or document it came from.

post.summary: My records of a type, by their fields
post.description: Up to five conditions on the fields the type declares (`eq`, `in`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `prefix`, `exists`), all of which must hold, words in the title, and the case they are filed under. Ordered by a declared field -- records with no value for it last -- or by `updated_at`, newest first when `order_by` is left out; the cursor belongs to that order. Read through the same visibility as the list: on a person's behalf, only what that person may see. A field the type does not declare, or a comparison its kind cannot take, is `422 plugin.record_field_unknown`.

get.summary: A file a person handed me
get.description: Needs `files.read`. A file the person picked for this installation in Korsi's file picker (the Bridge's `pickFile`), read on their behalf or by the installation itself. Any other file is `404 plugin.file_not_granted`.

get.summary: The bytes of a file a person handed me
get.description: Needs `files.read`. The bytes as the person gave them, streamed, always as an attachment. `media_type` is what Korsi read them as -- for showing, never for trusting.

get.summary: The text of a file a person handed me
get.description: Needs `files.read`. Read by Korsi from the file itself: plain text, Word, Excel, OpenDocument sheets, PowerPoint and a PDF's own text layer (`extraction: local`). A scan -- a PDF or a picture with no text of its own -- is read by OCR, a paid service only with `models.use`, billed to the publisher as `plugin.ocr`: the first ask queues it and answers `409 plugin.text_pending` (`retry_after_seconds` in its params), and once read every ask answers its text (`extraction: ocr`) at no further cost. `402 plugin.publisher_funds` while the publisher's paid services are paused. Otherwise `409 plugin.text_unavailable`, its `reason` saying why: `scan` (a scan, and no `models.use`), `ocr_unavailable` (this instance offers no OCR), `archive` (Korsi opens none: pick the files inside instead), `kind` (no text in it), `too_large` (past 25 MB, a zip that unpacks past what Korsi reads, a PDF past 500 pages, or more than a million characters of text) or `unreadable` (Korsi could not parse it, or OCR found no text in it).

post.summary: When these people are all free
post.description: Needs `calendar.read`, on a person's behalf only (`403 plugin.personal_needs_person` for the plugin acting as itself). Free times of `duration_minutes` when every one of `user_ids` -- active members, at most 20 -- is free, from `from` to `to` (both included, at most 31 days), inside the organization's working hours unless `within_hours` is false, and never on its days off or in the past. Times only: nothing about what anybody is doing. Nothing is booked.

get.summary: What is being said in a meeting I host
get.description: Needs `meetings.live.read`, a trusted scope. Only for a meeting this installation hosts, as itself or for a person who may see it: any other is `404 plugin.meeting_not_hosted`, and a restricted meeting another installation hosts is not found at all. Poll it: pass `covered_through` back as `since` for what came after. A preview, not the record -- the transcript read from the recording is, announced by `meeting.transcript_ready`.

get.summary: The language models Korsi lends me, and their price

post.summary: One answer from one of Korsi's models, at my publisher's cost
How loaded these colleagues are, day by day, as numbers
post.description: Needs `people.load.read`, on a person's behalf only (`403 plugin.personal_needs_person` for the plugin acting as itself). For each of `member_ids` (at most 200, each once) and each day from `from` to `to` (both included, at most 35 days, the organization's days): open and overdue tasks, their estimated minutes and how many carry none, meeting minutes inside working hours and the day's working minutes; and per colleague the open cases they own, those no colleague but them reads, the decisions waiting on them (with the day each started waiting) and those naming nobody but them. Numbers only, never a title; private work is counted. Answered for the person, everybody under them on the reporting line (`manager_member_id`, any depth) and, when they hold `member.load.read_all`, everybody; anybody else asked for is in `withheld`. In the order asked.

get.summary: The person's own single-person risk, item by item
get.description: Needs `people.load.read`, on a person's behalf only (`403 plugin.personal_needs_person` for the plugin acting as itself), and answers for that person alone: the followed (draft or open) cases they own that no colleague but them reads -- no observer, or private -- and the followed decisions naming nobody but them (as owner, sponsor, authority, approver or a recorded stakeholder), with titles, oldest first, at most 200 of each. The rows behind their own `cases_without_observer` and `single_person_decisions` in `POST /people/load`; anybody else's are numbers only.

post.summary: Put one card of proposals in front of the person you act for
post.description: On a person's behalf only (`403 plugin.personal_needs_person` for the plugin acting as itself). `changes` are 1 to 10 proposals, each with a `key`, a one-line `summary` in the person's language, `after` (earlier keys it builds on) and the proposal's `type`, `addressed_to` (that person, or a case they read) and `payload`, checked now as each would be applied (`422 plugin.proposal_invalid`). The card waits on the person's desk in «آماده برای شما»; they untick any change and confirm the rest with one press, or decline it. At most 30 cards wait on one desk (`409 plugin.cards_waiting`). Each proposal on a confirmed card is settled as `card:<card_id>:<key>`.

get.summary: One card your page put in front of somebody, and what became of it

AcceptProposal.title: AcceptProposal
AcceptProposal.description:
Accepting, optionally with the person's edits. An empty body applies the proposal as sent.

Each edit is for its own kind only, and at most one is given: a body for another kind is
refused (``plugin.proposal_edits_not_allowed``).

ActionItem.title: ActionItem
ActionItem.description: A piece of work somebody owns.

ActionPage.title: ActionPage
ActionPage.description: A page of actions. It may hold fewer than ``limit`` and still have a next page.

ActionScope.title: ActionScope
ActionScope.description:
Whose work this is, for reporting and for visibility.

Personal actions are modelled from the start even though they are out of scope for
this phase's UI, because retrofitting a scope onto a table that assumed everything
was organizational would mean a migration and a backfill over live work.

ActionStatus.title: ActionStatus
ActionStatus.description:
Where a piece of work is.

``WAITING`` and ``BLOCKED`` are separate because they need different responses:
waiting is somebody else's turn and resolves on its own, blocked needs an
intervention. Collapsing them is how work sits still while looking like it is
progressing.

AddressKind.title: AddressKind
AddressKind.description: Whom a proposal is put in front of.

AdvanceStage.title: AdvanceStage
AdvanceStage.description:
Move the case to another stage — the next one unless ``to_stage_key`` names a different one.

**The gate is soft (ADR-0027).** Moving forward while the current stage has required checklist
items not ticked, or required work still open (ADR-0048), is refused unless ``override_reason``
says why it is right to go on anyway. With a reason it proceeds, and the reason and what was
unmet are written to the timeline. Moving back needs no reason: returning to an earlier stage is
a correction, not a shortcut. Documents never hold a stage back (ADR-0031).

**Entering a stage creates the work it plans** (ADR-0048), in this command's transaction, as the
advance dialog previewed it: ``planned_overrides`` carries what the person changed — a task left
out, another owner, another date. ``carry_over`` moves open work of the stage being left into
the new one, completes it, or cancels it with ``cancel_reason``. Work completed in the same move
no longer holds the stage it is leaving.

Authority.title: Authority
Authority.description: Whose authority a plugin request carries (section 8).

BlockerStatus.title: BlockerStatus
BlockerStatus.description:
A blocker ends by being resolved or dismissed, never by being deleted.

``DISMISSED`` is not the same as ``RESOLVED``: one means the obstacle was removed, the
other that it turned out not to be one. Losing that distinction makes a case's history
read as though every problem got solved.

CalendarItem.title: CalendarItem
CalendarItem.description:
An event, or a dated record shown on the calendar (an action due, a case's review).

``withheld`` is an event the caller may know is there but not read: its time only.

CalendarPage.title: CalendarPage
CalendarPage.description:
A window of the calendar.

``truncated`` means the window held more than one answer carries: ask again from
``resume_from``.

CarryOver.title: CarryOver
CarryOver.description: One piece of the stage's open work, and what to do with it as the case moves on.

CarryOverChoice.title: CarryOverChoice
CarryOverChoice.description:
What happens to open work of the stage being left, when somebody says (ADR-0048).

Work nobody chose for stays where it was and is "carried over": still open, still in its stage.

CaseActivity.title: CaseActivity
CaseActivity.description: One thing that happened to a case. ``before``/``after`` hold the fields that changed.

CaseActivityKind.title: CaseActivityKind
CaseActivityKind.description: What happened to a case, for its timeline.

CaseAttention.title: CaseAttention
CaseAttention.description:
Whether the case is being looked after.

Computed on read from ownership, next step, dates and staleness — never stored. A
stored attention state is wrong the moment a deadline passes without anybody touching
the row, which is exactly the situation it is supposed to surface.

CaseDetail.title: CaseDetail
CaseDetail.description: ``GET /plugin/v1/cases/{id}``: a case and what it holds.

CaseFlowState.title: CaseFlowState
CaseFlowState.description:
How an open case is moving right now.

Only meaningful while the lifecycle is ``OPEN``; a resolved case has no flow. The
service enforces that rather than leaving a stale ``active`` on closed work, because a
dashboard counting ``active`` would otherwise include cases that finished months ago.

CaseHealth.title: CaseHealth
CaseHealth.description:
How the person accountable says the case is going.

Reported, never computed. Attention (``CaseAttention``) is what the dates and signals say; this
is the owner's judgement, which knows things no date does — that the customer went quiet, that
the budget is in doubt. The two are shown side by side precisely because they can disagree.

CaseItem.title: CaseItem
CaseItem.description: A case -- the unit the organization coordinates in -- as a list shows it.

CaseLifecycle.title: CaseLifecycle
CaseLifecycle.description:
Where the case is in its life.

``ARCHIVED`` is a filing state and not an outcome, which is why it is reachable only
from a case that has already been resolved, cancelled or merged: archiving instead of
resolving would record that the organization stopped looking at something without ever
saying how it ended.

``MERGED`` is its own outcome rather than a kind of cancellation. A duplicate filed into
another case was not abandoned -- its work goes on under the case it names in
``merged_into_id`` -- and reading it as "cancelled" told the people who opened it that the
organization had dropped the matter. Like the other closed states it is not tracked, so it
carries no signals and no deadline; unlike them it cannot be reopened, because the work it
held now lives in another case and two live copies of it is the state merging removed.

CaseLink.title: CaseLink
CaseLink.description:
Something filed under the case: a meeting, a document, a message, a link.

``target_id`` is the meeting's or the document's id when it is one, readable on its own route.

CaseNoteCategory.title: CaseNoteCategory
CaseNoteCategory.description:
What kind of statement a note on a case is (ADR-0020).

Kept from the vocabulary of the product this replaces, unchanged, because these are the
words the people doing this work already use.

Deliberately **not** merged with :class:`ContextRelationship`. That enum qualifies a *link*
to something stored elsewhere — evidence for, discussed in — while this says what the note
itself does. One is a relationship, the other a speech act, and a merged list would offer a
writer ``discussed_in`` and ``risk`` as alternatives to each other.

``BACKGROUND`` is the one that earns the whole feature: it is where an organization records
the history of a case that existed before Korsi did.

``DECISION`` records that a choice **was** made, so the case explains itself later. A choice
still being weighed belongs in the Decisions register, where it gets options, criteria and an
authority — this is a record, that is a process.

CasePriority.title: CasePriority
CasePriority.description:
How much the outcome matters.

Distinct from attention: a normal-priority case that nobody has touched for two months
needs attention, and a critical one that was reviewed yesterday does not.

CaseStage.title: CaseStage
CaseStage.description:
One stage of the case's process, in order (ADR-0084).

``key`` is what a ``case.stage.move`` names and ``operation.case.stage_moved`` reports: for a
case a plugin's ``case.create`` opened without a template, the key that plugin gave the stage,
and a key Korsi gave a stage the plugin brought without one or a person added. ``name`` is the
organization's, as ``stage_name`` is. ``position`` is 1-based; ``current`` marks the stage the
case is in, the one ``stage_key`` names, and no stage once the case has none.

CaseStatusUpdate.title: CaseStatusUpdate
CaseStatusUpdate.description: What the case's owner reported about it, newest first.

CaseType.title: CaseType
CaseType.description:
A coarse category, for defaults and filtering.

Not a module and not a workflow: every type shares one lifecycle. The value exists so
a tenant can see their sales cases separately, not so the system can behave
differently.

ChangeStatus.title: ChangeStatus
ChangeStatus.description: What became of one change on a confirmed card.

label.title: Label
label.description: Display name, or the email address when no name is set.

Colleague.title: Colleague
Colleague.description:
One person in this tenant, as a picker or a label needs them.

The shape every "who is this" question in the product resolves to. It exists because four
domains were each building it from ``app_user`` joined to ``tenant_member``, and a fifth was
about to: an owner picker in Operations, a voice picker in Meetings, an allocation picker in
Commerce, and actor labels in analysis views. Four copies of one query is four chances to
forget the status filter, and one of them had.

``label`` is resolved server-side rather than sent as a name plus an email for the client to
choose between. Which one to show is one decision -- display name, or the address when nobody
has set one -- and making it here is what stops two screens showing the same person
differently.

``status`` is carried rather than filtered out, because the two questions this answers want
opposite things. A picker offers only active members: a removed colleague must not be
assignable. A label must resolve for anybody, including somebody who has left, or a case they
used to own loses its history the day their account closes.

Consume.title: Consume
Consume.description: Hold and settle in one call, for a service that is done the moment it is asked for.

ContextLinkType.title: ContextLinkType
ContextLinkType.description:
What kind of thing a Context link points at.

Deliberately open-ended and mostly external: a case links to a provider file, a URL, a
message or another case. The type is stored so a link can be upgraded in place rather than
re-created when the pipeline behind its kind lands.

``MEETING`` and ``DOCUMENT`` are the two kinds this table no longer stores. They are still
members because rows written before the ingestion contexts existed carry them, and because
the case view speaks one vocabulary whichever store a related item came from -- see
:data:`ASSIGNED_CONTEXT_KINDS`.

DayLoad.title: DayLoad
DayLoad.description:
One colleague's day, as numbers.

A task falls on its due day; an overdue one on today, so a day before today carries no tasks.
``meeting_minutes`` are busy minutes inside the day's working window, so a day off has none.
``working_minutes`` are the organization's schedule for the day (zero on a day off), scaled by
the colleague's ``weekly_hours`` when the staff list has them. Leave is not subtracted.

DecisionExecutionState.title: DecisionExecutionState
DecisionExecutionState.description:
Whether the choice has actually been carried out.

Separate from :class:`DecisionState` because the two fail independently: a decision can
be recorded and never executed, which is one of the most useful signals the register
produces.

DecisionFollowUpRead.title: DecisionFollowUpRead
DecisionFollowUpRead.description:
One follow-up of a decision the reading plugin proposed, and where it stands (ADR-0096).

``result`` is what it made once applied: ``action_id``, ``case_id`` (an onboarding case the
plugin files its record under), ``member_id`` and ``user_id`` (the new colleague).

DecisionItem.title: DecisionItem
DecisionItem.description: A decision the organization is making, has made, or is carrying out.

DecisionLifecycle.title: DecisionLifecycle
DecisionLifecycle.description:
Whether the organization is still following this decision.

``ARCHIVED`` is a filing state and not an outcome, reachable only from a closed case —
the same rule as an Operational Case, and for the same reason: archiving instead of
closing would record that the organization stopped looking at a choice without ever
saying what it chose.

DecisionOutcome.title: DecisionOutcome
DecisionOutcome.description: What was decided, once it was: the statement as recorded and the option chosen.

DecisionOutcomeState.title: DecisionOutcomeState
DecisionOutcomeState.description: What the decision produced, once it is measurable.

DecisionState.title: DecisionState
DecisionState.description:
How far the reasoning has got.

Only meaningful while the lifecycle is ``DRAFT`` or ``OPEN``. The sequence is not
enforced as a strict pipeline: real decisions go back to ``framing`` when the question
turns out to be wrong, and a model that forbade that would be describing a process
nobody follows.

DecisionType.title: DecisionType
DecisionType.description: A coarse category, for defaults, filtering and approval expectations.

DocumentItem.title: DocumentItem
DocumentItem.description: A document, with no text from it: that is ``/documents/{id}/text``.

DocumentText.title: DocumentText
DocumentText.description: ``GET /plugin/v1/documents/{id}/text``: the text Korsi read out of it, as it reads now.

EmploymentType.title: EmploymentType
EmploymentType.description: How somebody works here, as the staff list says (ADR-0095). Never a contract's legal kind.

EntryKind.title: EntryKind
EntryKind.description:
Where a row on the calendar came from.

Load-bearing rather than decorative: an ``EVENT`` is the calendar's own record and opens its
editor, while every other kind is a date belonging to something else and opens that object's
page. Collapsing them would mean a click whose destination depends on data the client cannot
see.

``EVENT`` was ``provider_event`` while the events were somebody else's.

Never stored and never constrained in the database: it is computed per read, so adding a kind
is a value here and nothing else.

EventStatus.title: EventStatus
EventStatus.description:
Where an event stands.

``CANCELLED`` is why an enum earns its place over a boolean. A cancelled meeting is not a
deleted one: the slot was taken, somebody may have planned around it, and the honest thing to
show is a cancelled entry rather than an empty afternoon. Deleting the row asserts it never
existed.

ExtractionState.title: ExtractionState
ExtractionState.description:
How far Korsi has got with reading one document.

``EXTRACTING`` is worth its own state rather than being folded into ``PENDING``.
Reaching it means an external task exists and has been paid for, so a retry must
resume that task instead of creating a second one — and a reader watching the page
needs to be told the difference between "queued behind other work" and "the OCR
service has it now".

location.title: Location
location.description: Dotted path to the offending field.

FieldOperator.title: FieldOperator
FieldOperator.description: How one condition of a record query compares a field (ADR-0085).

FindFreeSlots.title: FindFreeSlots
FindFreeSlots.description:
``POST /plugin/v1/calendar/free-slots``: times when every one of these people is free.

Only on a person's handle, under ``calendar.read``. The answer is times, never what fills
anybody's day, and asking books nothing. The days are the organization's, in its time zone;
its days off are left out.

FreeSlotPage.title: FreeSlotPage
FreeSlotPage.description: The free times found, spread over the days searched.

HostMeeting.title: HostMeeting
HostMeeting.description:
``POST /plugin/v1/meetings``: a meeting the plugin hosts, created by the person in front of
it (``meetings.host``, a trusted scope, ADR-0083).

Only on a person's handle: that person creates it, and must be able to open ``case_id`` to file
it there. It is held in Korsi's own room, which the plugin's page opens with the Bridge's
``korsi:show``. The same ``external_id`` from the same installation answers the meeting already
made. The answer is the meeting as ``GET /meetings/{id}`` shows it.

Who is expected is its attendees, as on Korsi's own meeting form: the participants by id, then
the guests by name.

HostedGuest.title: HostedGuest
HostedGuest.description:
Somebody expected at a hosted meeting who is not a member -- an interview's candidate.

A name and nothing else. It is written on the meeting as an attendee known by name alone
(ADR-0027), the way Korsi's own form writes a name typed for somebody without an account. It
grants nothing: a restricted meeting is still read only by its member participants, the people
of its case and its host. There is no email and no phone, because Korsi invites nobody from it
and the plugin keeps the person's data.

HostedRecording.title: HostedRecording
HostedRecording.description:
How a hosted meeting is recorded, and how long Korsi keeps what it records.

The days are counted from the meeting's end. The organization's own retention ceiling caps
them, and the consent card shows the smaller. Left out, the audio or the words are kept as any
meeting's are.

InitialStep.title: InitialStep
InitialStep.description:
One piece of work named while capturing a case.

Becomes a real Action in the Actions context, linked to the case, in the same transaction as the
case itself. It used to be a sequence the browser ran — create the case, then each Action, then
each link — so a failure half way left a case with some of its steps, and pressing "save" again
made a second case.

IntakeSource.title: IntakeSource
IntakeSource.description: A message or a document a plugin brings in. It waits for a person's review (ADR-0006).

JsonSchemaFormat.title: JsonSchemaFormat
JsonSchemaFormat.description: The schema a ``json_schema`` answer must match, in the shape the model providers take.

LiveSegment.title: LiveSegment
LiveSegment.description:
One stretch of speech heard while the meeting is held: a preview, not the record. The
transcript made from the recording afterwards is the record (``meeting.transcript_ready``).

**Shaped as the Bridge's line, not as Korsi's room's.** The room's own segment carries the
engine's label, the track it came from and offsets measured per track, and the room names
voices from its roster beside it; a plugin has no roster to read, so the line comes named, as
the room shows it, and as ``korsi:meeting.live`` pushes it to the plugin's panel. The offsets
and tracks stay behind: they cannot be compared across participants, and ``at`` orders.

LiveTranscript.title: LiveTranscript
LiveTranscript.description:
``GET /plugin/v1/meetings/{id}/live/transcript?since=``: what has been said so far in a
meeting this installation hosts (``meetings.live.read``, a trusted scope, ADR-0083).

Polled, like Korsi's own room, and answered from the same reading
(``live_insight.transcript_view``): the newest room session, and the same cursor -- pass
``covered_through`` back as ``since`` and the answer holds only what came after it. Only each
line is shaped for a plugin (:class:`LiveSegment`).

LocalizedText.title: LocalizedText
LocalizedText.description:
A name or a sentence in the languages Korsi ships. At least one is required.

Persian first, because it is the default language of the product; any one is accepted so a
publisher writing in one language is not refused, and the store falls back through
:meth:`pick`.

MailAddress.title: MailAddress
MailAddress.description: One party to a message, as the mailbox shows it.

MailAttachment.title: MailAttachment
MailAttachment.description: An attachment's name and size. Its content does not come in with the message.

MailDetail.title: MailDetail
MailDetail.description: ``GET /plugin/v1/mail/{source_id}``: one message, its headers and its words.

MailHeaders.title: MailHeaders
MailHeaders.description:
What a message is beyond its text: who, when, where it sits and how it threads (ADR-0067).

Kept beside the source so a person's mail can be read as mail -- by thread, by sender -- and so
a mailbox that moves or deletes a message can be followed: ``provider_item_id`` and ``folder``
are the mailbox's own address for it, which changes when it moves.

MailItem.title: MailItem
MailItem.description: One message a person's connection brought in, as a list shows it.

MeetingItem.title: MeetingItem
MeetingItem.description: A meeting, with no words from it: those are ``/meetings/{id}/transcript``.

MeetingState.title: MeetingState
MeetingState.description:
Where a Korsi meeting has got to.

``AWAITING_RECORDING`` is the state a meeting created from a calendar entry sits in, and the
state a meeting returns to if its only recording is detached. Distinct from ``PENDING``
extraction: there is nothing to process yet, as opposed to something queued.

MeetingTranscript.title: MeetingTranscript
MeetingTranscript.description: ``GET /plugin/v1/meetings/{id}/transcript``: what was said, as it reads now.

MembershipStatus.title: MembershipStatus
MembershipStatus.description:
Whether a user may act inside a tenant.

``REMOVED`` rather than deleting the row: membership history is what makes an
audit entry from last year legible, and re-adding somebody must not silently
revive whatever their old roles were.

MemoryAnswer.title: MemoryAnswer
MemoryAnswer.description:
The result of a memory search.

``dropped_unresolved`` and ``dropped_quarantined`` are reported separately because they mean
different things to an operator: the first suggests drift between Korsi and the provider,
the second is the system correctly withholding a source that is mid-synchronisation.

``facts`` lists every fact that passed the relevance cut first, then the weakly related ones
flagged ``low_relevance``. An answer whose facts are all flagged is memory saying it has nothing
that answers this question -- which is an answer, and not the same one as an empty list.

id.title: Id
id.description: Provider fact id. Opaque; useful for feedback and tracing.

MemoryFactView.title: MemoryFactView
MemoryFactView.description: One statement from memory, with its provenance resolved.

MemoryLayer.title: MemoryLayer
MemoryLayer.description:
How settled a piece of knowledge is.

Korsi's own categories. The adapter maps these onto whatever the engine calls them,
which is what keeps the provider's vocabulary out of every caller.

MemorySearchRequest.title: MemorySearchRequest
MemorySearchRequest.description: A question put to organizational memory.

MemorySourceRef.title: MemorySourceRef
MemorySourceRef.description:
Where a fact came from, resolved against Korsi rather than trusted from the provider.

Every field here is read from Korsi's own tables after the provider answers. The provider's
metadata is not used for any of it: it is data the provider returns, so treating it as proof
of provenance would make a bank misconfiguration a cross-tenant leak.

MemorySyncState.title: MemorySyncState
MemorySyncState.description:
Where this source stands with the provider.

``UNKNOWN`` is the state this enum exists for. Every other value is a fact; ``UNKNOWN``
records the absence of one, which is exactly what a timed-out retain leaves behind when
the provider accepts no caller-supplied operation id. Folding it into ``FAILED`` would
invite a retry that could extract the same source twice; folding it into ``APPLIED``
would expose facts nobody verified.

ModelCompletion.title: ModelCompletion
ModelCompletion.description: The model's answer, and what it cost the publisher.

OpenHold.title: OpenHold
OpenHold.description: Reserve MU before a service, at the active plan's rate (section 16).

OptionKind.title: OptionKind
OptionKind.description: The shape of a course of action.

OptionStatus.title: OptionStatus
OptionStatus.description:
Where an option stands.

``NOT_CONSIDERED_AT_TIME`` is the one that matters historically: an option discovered
afterwards must be recordable without making it look as though it was on the table.

Organization.title: Organization
Organization.description:
``GET /plugin/v1/org``: the organization as it has recorded itself, and its chart.

Every field is empty until the organization records its profile -- a fresh organization has no
legal name yet, and that is an answer rather than an error.

OrganizationMember.title: OrganizationMember
OrganizationMember.description:
A colleague as the organization's staff list records them (ADR-0095).

``user_id`` is how the colleague appears everywhere else on this plane -- an owner, an assignee,
the colleague a decision is about -- and every member has one; ``has_login`` says whether they
sign in to Korsi, because one who does not has no calendar. ``manager_member_id`` is the
reporting line: the ``member_id`` of the colleague they report to, which may be somebody no
longer in the list.

The five facts of how they work here are all optional, and empty means "not given": no
probation date means the start plus the plugin's default, no hours mean the organization's work
schedule. ``leave_days_ahead`` counts days of leave in the four weeks after ``leave_as_of``;
past those four weeks the count is stale and counts as zero.

Never here: the personnel number, the place of work, and anything of a personnel file -- a
salary, a national id, a birth date, an address. Korsi does not keep those at all.

OrganizationPerson.title: OrganizationPerson
OrganizationPerson.description: A person in the organization's chart. ``user_id`` is set when they use Korsi.

OrganizationUnit.title: OrganizationUnit
OrganizationUnit.description: A unit of the organization's chart, as recorded today.

OrganizationalUnitKind.title: OrganizationalUnitKind
OrganizationalUnitKind.description:
What kind of structure a unit is.

A closed, deliberately short list. The temptation is to let each tenant name its own levels, and
that is what the custom-object platform is for; a unit kind is read by product logic, so an open
vocabulary would make it unusable for anything but display.

PageCardChange.title: PageCardChange
PageCardChange.description: One change on a card from the plugin's own page: a proposal, so ``kind`` may be left out.

ParticipantRole.title: ParticipantRole
ParticipantRole.description: Somebody's part in the case, beyond the single owner.

PeopleLoadPage.title: PeopleLoadPage
PeopleLoadPage.description:
The colleagues answered for, in the order asked, and the ones left out.

``withheld`` names every ``member_id`` asked for that is not answered: out of the person's
reach (not them, not under them on the reporting line, and they do not hold
``member.load.read_all``) or no active colleague here. The two are not told apart.

PeopleLoadQuery.title: PeopleLoadQuery
PeopleLoadQuery.description:
``POST /plugin/v1/people/load``: how loaded these colleagues are, day by day, as numbers.

Only on a person's handle, under ``people.load.read``. Colleagues by ``member_id`` (from
``GET /org/members``), each named once; the days are the organization's, in its time zone, both
ends included.

PersonLoad.title: PersonLoad
PersonLoad.description:
One colleague's load (ADR-0095 decision 4). **Numbers only**: no title, no id of any record.

The totals are today's, whatever days were asked: every open task assigned to them, private
ones included, with ``actions_without_due_date`` counted on no day; the cases they own that are
still followed, and those no colleague but them reads (no observer, or private); the decisions
waiting on them as authority or approver -- ``decisions_waiting_since`` is the day each started
waiting, oldest first -- and the followed decisions naming nobody but them.

``has_calendar`` is false for a colleague who does not sign in: they have no calendar of their
own, so a plugin says so instead of showing an empty week. Events and meetings that name them
still count in ``meeting_minutes``.

PlannedOverride.title: PlannedOverride
PlannedOverride.description:
The person's choice for one planned task of the stage being entered (ADR-0048).

``create=False`` sets the task aside (``dismissed``) instead of creating it. ``assignee_id``
and ``due_at`` count only when they are sent: ``null`` means unassigned or no due date, and
leaving a field out keeps what the plan's rule gives — the value the dialog previewed.

PluginCardEdits.title: PluginCardEdits
PluginCardEdits.description:
What the person changed on one of a card's changes before confirming it (ADR-0080 decision
5, as ADR-0068 has it for a proposal): an action's arguments, or a proposal in Korsi's own
form.

PluginCardView.title: PluginCardView
PluginCardView.description:
A card the plugin's page put in front of a person, as the plugin reads it back.

``pending`` while it waits; ``applied`` when one change or more applied, ``failed`` when none
did, ``rejected`` when the person declined it. ``changes`` is what became of each change, in
the card's order, once it was confirmed (empty while it waits and when it was declined).

PluginChangeOutcome.title: PluginChangeOutcome
PluginChangeOutcome.description: What became of one change on a confirmed card, and what it produced.

PluginEventView.title: PluginEventView
PluginEventView.description: One event in an installation's stream: thin, with ids, never content (section 13).

PluginFile.title: PluginFile
PluginFile.description:
``GET /plugin/v1/files/{id}``: a file a person picked for this installation in Korsi's own
file picker (``files.read``). While the installation uses it, its owner removing it only
archives it. Any other file of theirs is not found.

PluginFileText.title: PluginFileText
PluginFileText.description:
``GET /plugin/v1/files/{id}/text``: the text Korsi read out of a file it was handed. A file
with no text Korsi may read -- a scan without ``models.use``, an archive -- answers
``plugin.text_unavailable``.

PluginModel.title: PluginModel
PluginModel.description: A language model Korsi lets trusted plugins use, and what it costs the publisher.

PluginRecordRef.title: PluginRecordRef
PluginRecordRef.description: One of the plugin's own records, by the plugin's own keys for it.

PluginSelf.title: PluginSelf
PluginSelf.description: ``GET /plugin/v1/installation``: who the plugin is talking as, and what it may do.

title.title: Title
title.description: Message rendered in the caller's locale.

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable machine-readable error code and i18n key.

params.title: Params
params.description: Typed values the client may use to render its own message.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Correlates this response with server logs.

examples.title: You do not have permission to do this.

ProposalActionEdits.title: ProposalActionEdits
ProposalActionEdits.description:
What the person changed on an ``action.create`` before applying it: Korsi's own new-action
form, opened filled in with the plugin's proposal, as they saved it.

A field left out keeps the plugin's value; ``null`` clears an assignee, a date or an estimate.
The action is still the plugin's proposal applied -- marked as its work, the proposal settled
and the plugin told -- only with the person's words. The fields are the form's: what
``CreateAction`` takes from a person.

ProposalCaseEdits.title: ProposalCaseEdits
ProposalCaseEdits.description:
What the person changed on a ``case.create`` before applying it: Korsi's new-case form,
opened filled in with the plugin's proposal, as they saved it (ADR-0084).

A field left out keeps the plugin's value; ``null`` clears a description, a target date or a
template, and an owner left ``null`` is the person accepting. The case is still the plugin's
proposal applied -- its origin recorded, the proposal settled and the plugin told -- only with
the person's words. The fields are the form's.

**The people involved are the person's to change too.** ``participants`` replaces the plugin's
list whole: whoever the person took off is never added, and whoever they added is, as
``add_participant`` adds anybody. On a confidential case they are its readers, so who reads it
is the person's choice, not the plugin's. ``[]`` involves nobody beside the owner.

ProposalStatus.title: ProposalStatus
ProposalStatus.description: ADR-0014's lifecycle, as far as a plugin's proposal travels it.

ProposalType.title: ProposalType
ProposalType.description: What a plugin may propose into Korsi's own records (section 11).

ProposedCaseParticipant.title: ProposedCaseParticipant
ProposedCaseParticipant.description: Somebody a proposed case involves beside its owner, with their part in it.

PutRecord.title: PutRecord
PutRecord.description: Write one of the plugin's own records, keyed by the plugin's own id for it.

QueryRecords.title: QueryRecords
QueryRecords.description:
``POST /plugin/v1/records/{type}/query``: the plugin's records of a type, by their fields
(ADR-0085).

Every condition must hold. The query is always read through the reader's own filter -- the
type's visibility and its ``read_permission`` -- so it never shows a reader a record a list of
the same type would not. Ordered by a field, the cursor carries that field's value and the
record's id; records with no value for it come last.

RecordCondition.title: RecordCondition
RecordCondition.description: One condition of a record query: a declared field, how to compare it, and with what.

RecordOrder.title: RecordOrder
RecordOrder.description: What a record query is ordered by: a declared field, or when the record last changed.

RecordProposedDecision.title: RecordProposedDecision
RecordProposedDecision.description:
Recording a full ``decision.candidate`` in the same save that accepts it (ADR-0096).

Korsi's own record-decision form, opened on the candidate for the person who is its decider,
as they saved it: the option by the plugin's key, and the rest as ``record_decision`` takes it.
Applied after the decision is created, through the register's own handler, so every refusal
the decision page makes -- not the decider, a consequential choice without a review date, no
evidence and no reason -- is made here, and the proposal then stays pending for the person.

RecordVisibility.title: RecordVisibility
RecordVisibility.description: Who sees a plugin's record of a given type (decision 17).

RecordingConsent.title: RecordingConsent
RecordingConsent.description: Whether Korsi asks for consent before a hosted meeting is recorded (ADR-0083).

RequestCompletion.title: RequestCompletion
RequestCompletion.description:
``POST /plugin/v1/models/complete``: one answer from one of Korsi's models (ADR-0081).

Korsi calls the model itself, down the path its own calls take, so the organization's data goes
nowhere it does not go already, and the plugin brings no key. The call is metered with its
dollar cost, paid by the publisher -- never the organization -- and ``purpose`` is recorded
beside it. The same ``idempotency_key`` from the same installation answers the first call's
answer again rather than paying twice: the first answer is replayed for an hour, and a key
reused for a different request is ``request.invalid``. Not streamed.

Reversibility.title: Reversibility
Reversibility.description:
How hard it would be to undo.

Drives how much analysis and approval the domain expects: an irreversible decision with
one option and no approval is refused, while a reversible one is not.

RiskCase.title: RiskCase
RiskCase.description: A followed case the person owns that no colleague but them reads: no observer, or private.

RiskDecision.title: RiskDecision
RiskDecision.description:
A followed decision on which nobody but the person is named -- as owner, sponsor, authority,
approver or a recorded stakeholder.

SinglePersonRisk.title: SinglePersonRisk
SinglePersonRisk.description:
``GET /plugin/v1/people/single-person-risk``: the rows behind the person's own
``cases_without_observer`` and ``single_person_decisions`` (design §8ب.4), **for the person
themself alone** -- their handover list. Everybody else is told the numbers only, by
``POST /people/load``. Oldest first; at most 200 of each, ``more_*`` true when there are more.

SkipReason.title: SkipReason
SkipReason.description: Why a change on a confirmed card was not attempted.

SourceConsent.title: SourceConsent
SourceConsent.description: Who agreed to this material reaching Korsi, through which channel.

StageDraft.title: StageDraft
StageDraft.description:
One stage in a list somebody arranged: a stage that exists, by key, or a new one, by name.

``key`` names a stage the list already had — the case's own, or the template's at creation — and
a draft that carries one keeps that stage's identity: its key, its checklist, its history. A
draft without a key is a new stage and is given a fresh key by the server; keys are identifiers,
never shown, so the person arranging the list never has to invent one.

``name`` left out keeps the stage's current name — which, for a built-in stage, is a
translation the client showed rather than text anybody typed. Given, it replaces the name and
the stage stops being translated: it is now in the words of the person who wrote it.

SubmitPluginCard.title: SubmitPluginCard
SubmitPluginCard.description:
``POST /plugin/v1/cards``: changes to Korsi's own records that belong together, put in front
of one person as **one card** from the plugin's own page (plugin API 1.9) -- a leaving
colleague's handovers, say, confirmed once instead of one by one.

**On a person's handle only, for that person.** The card waits on their desk in «آماده برای
شما» (like an outside assistant's), from the plugin by name and mark; they may untick any change
and confirm the rest with one press, or decline it. Each change is a proposal the plugin may
make -- a type its manifest declares, under a scope it was given, addressed to that person or to
a case they may decide on -- and is checked now as it would be applied. Confirming submits each
and accepts it as the person, in the card's order, each on its own; a change that fails is named
on the card and the others stay applied. Every proposal on it reaches the plugin as
``plugin.proposal.settled`` with ``external_id`` ``card:<card_id>:<key>``.

Counted as one proposal against the installation's proposals budget, and toward its acceptance
rate once, as a specialist's card is (ADR-0080 decision 7).

SubmitProposal.title: SubmitProposal
SubmitProposal.description: The one envelope every plugin proposal arrives in (section 11).

TextExtraction.title: TextExtraction
TextExtraction.description: How Korsi read a file's text.

WalletView.title: WalletView
WalletView.description: An installation's wallet: the third layer of the organization's credit (decision 4).
